findings.reason: Trace step 9 shows player-2-legend-ogn-251-298's conditional-draw trigger on the chain while player-2 holds 5 cards; step 10 (Pass) resolves it and player-2's hand goes 5->6 (Gust Monk). Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/loose-cannon.ts:12-16) uses condition {type:'count', target:{controller:'friendly', location:'hand', type:'card'}, comparison:{lte:1}}. evaluateEffectCondition 'count' (_helpers.ts:234-256) computes n via resolveTarget (line 244) for non-rune targets. resolveTarget (target-resolver.ts:95, 190-215) only gathers board cards from base + battlefield zones via getBoardCardIds and has no location:'hand' branch (lines 135-165 handle only here/base/move-to-or-from/battlefield*); furthermore lines 183-184 slice to quantity 1 by default, so n is always <= 1 and the lte:1 check always passes. findings.why_wrong: Rule 335/334.2/336: the game may only 'proceed to the next substep, step, phase, or turn' when there are no Outstanding Tasks AND no pending Chain Items; pending items must be processed via FEPR first. Channel and Draw must not happen until the Beginning-phase chain is empty. This materially breaks Loose Cannon (ogn-251-298): per 383.2.a.1 its 'one or fewer cards in hand' check happens at resolution, which is supposed to be before the Draw Phase draw; resolving it after the draw evaluates against a hand that is one card larger, so the legend will systematically fail to draw when it should (hand of 1 at Beginning becomes 2 by resolution).
findings.reason: riftbound-flow.ts:242-244 defines the `beginning` phase with `endIf: () => true, next: "channel"` — unconditional auto-advance. Its onBegin (line 297) calls fireTriggers({type:"start-of-turn"}, buildFlowTriggerContext(context)); buildFlowTriggerContext (lines 40-80) does not set resolveInline, so per trigger-runner.ts:425-459 the Loose Cannon trigger is pushed onto the chain via addToChain and left pending. Because beginning's endIf ignores chain state, the FlowManager immediately runs channel.onBegin (line 344, channels runes), draw.onBegin (line 442, draws 1 card), draw.onEnd (line 450-457, empties rune pool) and main.onBegin (phase='main') with chain-1 still unresolved. Contrast the `ending` phase at lines 495-497, which explicitly gates endIf on `!interaction.chain.active && !pendingChoice` — the beginning phase lacks this guard. Trace step 9 matches: chain-1 (start-of-turn conditional count-hand<=1 → draw) pending while turn.phase='main' and the draw already happened, so the hand-size condition is evaluated post-draw.

findings.what: No target selection when multiple legal targets exist
findings.expected: 'Deal 2 to a unit at a battlefield' is a caster-chosen target; with Blazing Scorcher and Legion Rearguard both at the battlefield the player should be prompted (per-target playSpell variants or a pendingChoice).
findings.observed: Enumerator offered a single playSpell with no targets param, no pendingChoice/prompt appeared in UI; engine silently picked Blazing Scorcher and killed it, Legion Rearguard untouched. (Root cause appears to be the sequence-shaped effect having no top-level target, so play-spell enumerator skips per-target enumeration.)
findings.reason: Registry abilities for sfd-017-221 (and ogn-213-298) are `{type:"spell", effect:{type:"sequence", effects:[{type:"damage",amount:2,target:{type:"unit",location:"battlefield"}}, ...]}}` — no top-level `effect.target`. In packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/play-spell.ts:233-241 the enumerator computes `tgt = spellEffect?.target ?? findAmountReferenceTarget(spellEffect)`; for a sequence both are undefined, so `isCardTarget` is false and control falls to the else branch at play-spell.ts:346-350 which pushes a single variant with no `targets`. (spellEffectHasLegalTargets at targeting.ts:109 does recurse into sequences, so the play is offered, but per-target enumeration never recurses.) At resolution the plain damage path (abilities/effects/damage.ts:155 getTargetIds → resolveTarget default first match) picks the first unit with no pendingChoice, matching the observed silent Blazing Scorcher pick.

findings.what: "Spend 2 XP" activated ability checks/pays a per-card `xp` counter on the unit instead of the player's XP pool (rules 729-730: XP is a player resource).
findings.expected: With player-1 XP = 3, activateAbility for Enthralling Protector (abilityIndex 3) should be offered; on activation player XP should drop 3 -> 1.
findings.observed: With players.player-1.xp = 3 the ability was not listed in moves and a direct activateAbility call was a no-op. It only became available after `addCounter {counterType:'xp', delta:2}` on the card itself; activation then removed the card's xp counters (2 -> 0) while player XP stayed at 3. (activate-ability.ts uses counters.getCounter(cardId,'xp') / removeCounter.)
findings.reason: activate-ability.ts:405-413 gates the "Spend N XP" cost on `getCounter(cardId, "xp")` (per-card counter) and activate-ability.ts:774-777 pays it via `counters.removeCounter(cardId, "xp", xpCost)`. Meanwhile gain-xp (abilities/effects/gain-xp.ts:9, operations/xp-operations.ts:31) stores XP on `draft.players[playerId].xp`, matching rules 729-730 (XP is marked on the Player; 730.2 Spend = reduce player's XP). So with player xp=3 and no card counters the ability is unaffordable, and paying drains card counters instead of player XP — exactly as observed.

findings.what: [Hunt] did not grant XP when the unit conquered a battlefield via a non-combat showdown.
findings.expected: After Enthralling Protector moved alone to empty Abandoned Hall and both players passed focus (battlefield controller -> player-1, VP 0 -> 1 = conquer), player-1 should gain 1 XP.
findings.observed: VP went 0 -> 1 and controller set to player-1, but player XP stayed 3 (and no xp counter added, no chain item). showdown.ts passShowdownFocus non-combat conquer path sets controller/VP but never emits a 'conquer' game event, and operations/hunt-keyword.ts getHuntValue is not called from anywhere.
findings.reason: showdown.ts:99-121 (passShowdownFocus reducer, non-combat close / rule 348.2.a path) sets bf.controller, pushes conqueredThisTurn/scoredThisTurn and increments victoryPoints directly, but never calls fireTriggeredAbilitiesForEvent with a {type:"conquer"} event (contrast conquer-battlefield.ts:161-164 and resolve-full-combat.ts:287-289 which do). After it sets controller, conquerBattlefield becomes illegal (conquer-battlefield.ts:56 `bf.controller === playerId -> false`), so no later move fires the event either. Enthralling Protector's [Hunt] is enriched by the parser into a triggered {event:"conquer", on:"self"} -> gain-xp ability, so it depends on that event. Reproduced with the rules-audit harness: unit with the Hunt conquer trigger moves alone to empty bf, both players passShowdownFocus -> VP 0->1, controller=player-1, xp stays 0, chain null; same unit via conquerBattlefield puts the gain-xp trigger on the chain. (Minor correction to the report: Hunt is wired via parser expansion, not operations/hunt-keyword.ts — getHuntValue/computeHuntXpGain are indeed dead code, but the root cause is the missing conquer event emission.)

findings.what: "Prevent all spell and ability damage this turn" has no effect.

findings.reason: Parser turns "Prevent all spell and ability damage this turn." into {type:"prevent-damage", amount:"all", duration:"turn"} with no target (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:204). handle_preventDamage (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/prevent-damage.ts:8-17) falls back to [ctx.sourceCardId] when targets is empty and only writes meta.damagePreventionShield. Repo-wide grep shows damagePreventionShield is written at prevent-damage.ts:15 and read nowhere; damage.ts:157-198 only consults checkReplacement (take-damage replacements) then applies counters/meta.damage; operations/prevent-damage.ts applyPrevent (line 43) has no callers. So the spell has no effect on subsequent spell damage.

findings.what: Damage amount: both the 'deal 2' and the 'deal 4 instead' clauses are applied unconditionally

findings.reason: Card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/sudden-storm.ts) has no explicit abilities, so the parser derives them. Running parseAbilities on the rulesText yields exactly the observed {type:'sequence', effects:[damage 2 unit@battlefield, damage 4 unit]} with no condition. Root cause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-conditional.ts:157-195 (parseCommaPronounChain), invoked from parser/impl/effects.ts:140 before sentence splitting. The text has 2+ pronouns and a comma, so it is split on ',' into 'Deal 2 to a unit at a battlefield. If it's attacking' and 'deal 4 to it instead'; each is fed to parseEffect (line 186), which parses them as plain damage 2 and damage 4, discarding the "If it's attacking" condition and the "instead" replacement semantics. Result: both damages apply unconditionally (6 total), killing a non-attacking 5-might unit.

findings.what: [Empowered] static '+2 Might and Ganking' never applies after Empower resolves

Root cause: parser emits the static ability as effect {type:'sequence', effects:[modify-might +2, grant-keyword Ganking]} with condition while-empowered, and static-abilities.ts applyPass only handles top-level effect types in PASS_1/PASS_2 sets (modify-might/grant-keyword), so a 'sequence' static effect is silently skipped.
findings.reason: Verified by running the parser on Brutal Hunter's rulesText: it yields {type:'static', condition:{type:'while-empowered'}, effect:{type:'sequence', effects:[{type:'modify-might',amount:2,target:'self'},{type:'grant-keyword',keyword:'Ganking'}]}} (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/gated.ts:173-181 wraps parseInner output; the 'I have' fast path at gated.ts:153 doesn't match '+2 [Might] and [Ganking]'). findings.what: Death trigger never fires
findings.expected: When another friendly non-Recruit unit dies, a 1-Might Recruit unit token is played into player-1's base
findings.observed: Killed a friendly Legion Rearguard with Vengeance (kill effect) and a second one with Falling Star (3 damage, lethal via SBA); both went to trash but no Viktor trigger appeared on the chain and no Recruit token was created either time — base contained only Viktor
findings.reason: Reproduced end-to-end with the rules-audit harness: Viktor's exact ability (and even a plain `on: "friendly-units"` die trigger) in P1 base + friendly unit; playSpell with a `kill` effect or a lethal 3-damage effect targeting the ally, then pass priority until the chain empties. In both cases the ally lands in trash, the chain goes empty with no triggered item ever added, and P1 base contains only Viktor. (A direct fireTrigger({type:"die"}) does match Viktor's object-shaped `on`, so the matcher is fine — the die event is simply never emitted.) Root causes: (1) SBA path — game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:250-255 (passChainPriority reducer) and :300-305 call `performCleanup(...)` directly and discard `result.killed`, so lethally-damaged units are moved to trash with no `dispatchUnitDied`/die event; `withPostMoveCleanup`/`cleanupAndFireDeaths` (cleanup/post-move-cleanup.ts:97) is defined but never applied to any move map, so nothing else emits it. (2) Kill-effect path — abilities/effects/kill.ts:6-14 `handle_kill` just does `ctx.zones.moveCard({targetZoneId:"trash"})` with no die event dispatch. Hence "when another friendly unit dies" triggers (Viktor ogn-246-298) never fire from spell kills or spell-damage deaths.

findings.expected: P1's Dazzling Aurora end-of-turn trigger reveals Akshan and plays him ignoring cost; P1 may still pay the optional [body][body] additional cost (rule 356.1.b.3), Akshan's play effect takes control of the enemy Dazzling Aurora; the stolen Aurora does NOT trigger that same turn, but DOES trigger at the end of P1's future turns while P1 controls it.
findings.observed: (1) Aurora's 'play it, ignoring its cost' is resolved as a raw zone move (reveal.ts adds a chain item {type:'move', to:'choose'} -> choose-destination -> zones.moveCard). Akshan simply entered base; no prompt to pay the optional [body][body] additional cost was offered (P1 had 2 body power floating), so his 'When you play me, if you paid the additional cost' steal can never happen via Aurora. Same for Legion Rearguard revealed later: no Accelerate option. (2) To test the timing claim anyway, I used sandbox transferControl to hand P2's Aurora to P1 during P1's ending phase (while P1's Aurora trigger was on the chain): it did not trigger that turn (superficially matches), BUT it then still triggered for its OWNER (P2) at the end of P2's next turn (played Punching Poro for P2), and at the end of P1's following turn only P1's original Aurora triggered (one reveal on chain, not two). Root cause: trigger-runner getBoardCards() scans base via zones.getCardsInZone('base', playerId), which filters by card.owner, and tags owner:playerId — 'At the end of your turn' is keyed on owner, not controller. So a control-changed Aurora never triggers for its new controller, contradicting 'it can trigger at the end of your future turns for as long as you control it'.
findings.notes: Setup: goldfish game bdfc49a6; tutored ogn-160-298 for P1 (played via playGear) and P2 (placed in base via sandbox duplicateCard since goldfish auto-ends turn), tutored sfd-109-221 and placed on top of P1 deck via placeCardsOnTopOfDeckInOrder, added 2 body power, endTurn, passed priority through chain. Two engine bugs: (a) packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/reveal.ts + pending-choice.ts choose-destination path does not run the play pipeline (no optional additional-cost payment per rule 356.1.b.3; likely no proper 'play' event either); (b) packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts getBoardCards uses owner instead of controller for base cards, so controller-relative turn triggers ignore control changes (affects Akshan's take-control generally). Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-56312d623221a2f8.png. Caveat: the scratchpad gid.txt was overwritten by a sibling agent mid-run, so one duplicateCard call (P2 Aurora into base) accidentally hit game 03869baa-91d8-4d1f-994c-73279db26ae2; I issued one /undo on that game to revert it, which appears to have also rolled back that game's internal zone state further than one move (tokens vanished) — possible separate undo-snapshot bug, and that sibling's game may have been disturbed.
